Parity held cleanly for the whole paper: ODD indices 1-21 are HINDI, EVEN indices 2-22 are ENGLISH, and it does NOT invert part-way. There is also NO cross-language overflow: each page continues onto the next page of its OWN language, so the English text at the top of idx 12 (Q22(b)) continues the English at the foot of idx 10, and nothing English sits on any odd page. Verified by accounting for all 24 indices and by checking that Q1-Q33 run unbroken with every sub-part present. DECIMAL POINTS ARE ORDINARY BASELINE FULL STOPS on this paper (checked at 5x on '0.5 A' idx 4, '0.1 mm'/'1.20 m' idx 20, and the constants block on idx 2) - no {\cdot} anywhere. MARKING SCHEME is 18 pages, headed 'PAPER CODE 55/1/3', i.e. already scoped to this paper alone; all 18 pages were read. 26 keyed MCQs: 16 in Section A + 10 in Section D (both case studies are MCQ, 5 sub-parts each incl. their OR branches). questions.stem: A charge Q is fixed in position. Another charge q is brought near charge Q and released from rest. Which of the following graphs is the correct representation of the acceleration of the charge q as a function of its distance r from charge Q ?

options.label: A
options.text: a plot of a (vertical axis) against r (horizontal axis) that starts at a high value close to the a-axis, falls steeply, and then flattens out towards the r-axis without reaching it

options.label: B
options.text: a plot of a (vertical axis) against r (horizontal axis) that begins at a high value and stays almost flat for a while, then drops steeply in an S-bend and levels off just above the r-axis

options.label: C
options.text: a plot of a (vertical axis) against r (horizontal axis) that is a straight line falling steadily from a high value on the a-axis to a low value at large r

options.label: D
options.text: a plot of a (vertical axis) against r (horizontal axis) that starts at zero, rises to a single rounded peak and then falls back close to the r-axis

questions._figure: REQUIRED - the four options ARE four drawn graphs and the printed paper gives them no text at all beyond the axis labels a and r. The option texts above are a plain reading of what each graph draws (which axis is which, the starting value, the shape); that reading is lossless, and choosing between them still requires knowing that the Coulomb force and hence the acceleration goes as 1/r^2, so nothing is handed over. questions.stem:

questions._flag: TRANSCRIBED AS PRINTED - the Reason's carrier symbols are set in GREEK ETA, not the Latin n a carrier number density is normally written with. Confirmed independently on THIS paper at 4x zoom (page idx 8): the glyph carries eta's descender and is plainly a different letter from the Latin 'n' in 'n-type' on the same line. So the printed Reason reads \(\eta_e \gg \eta_h\) / \(\eta_h \gg \eta_e\) and is transcribed that way rather than silently repaired to \(n_e\) / \(n_h\).

questions.subtopic: Magnetic Force and Motion in a Magnetic Field
questions.stem:
A particle of charge q is moving with a velocity \(\vec{v}\) at a distance 'd' from a long straight wire carrying a current 'I' as shown in figure. At this instant, it is subjected to a uniform electric field \(\vec{E}\) such that the particle keeps moving undeviated. In terms of unit vectors \(\hat{i}\), \(\hat{j}\) and \(\hat{k}\), find -
(a) the magnetic field \(\vec{B}\),
(b) the magnetic force \(\vec{F}_m\), and
(c) the electric field \(\vec{E}\), acting on the charge.
questions._figure: REQUIRED - the stem says 'as shown in figure' and every one of the three answers is a DIRECTED quantity whose sign comes only from the drawing. Described: a long horizontal straight line labelled 'Wire', dashed at both ends, carrying an arrowhead labelled I; above it, at a perpendicular separation marked by a shaded vertical bar with arrowheads and labelled d, a filled dot representing the charge, with a straight arrow labelled \(\vec{v}\) drawn from it; and, to the right of the whole arrangement, a separate axes triad with y drawn upwards, x drawn to the right and z drawn down-and-left towards the reader, carrying the unit vectors \(\hat{j}\), \(\hat{i}\) and \(\hat{k}\) along those three axes respectively. Deliberately WITHHELD: the SENSE of the current arrowhead along the wire and the SENSE of the velocity arrow - those two directions are exactly what fix the signs of \(\vec{B}\), \(\vec{F}_m\) and \(\vec{E}\), i.e. the whole of what the question asks for. questions.context:
A circuit consisting of a capacitor C, a resistor of resistance R and an ideal battery of emf V, as shown in figure is known as RC series circuit.
As soon as the circuit is completed by closing key \(\mathrm{S_1}\) (keeping \(\mathrm{S_2}\) open) charges begin to flow between the capacitor plates and the battery terminals. The charge on the capacitor increases and consequently the potential difference \(V_c\) (= q/C) across the capacitor also increases with time. When this potential difference equals the potential difference across the battery, the capacitor is fully charged (Q = VC). During this process of charging, the charge q on the capacitor changes with time t as
\(q = Q[1 - e^{-t/RC}]\)
The charging current can be obtained by differentiating it and using \(\frac{d}{dx}(e^{mx}) = m e^{mx}\).
Consider the case when R = 20 k\(\Omega\), C = 500 \(\mu\)F and V = 10 V.

questions.context:
A circuit consisting of a capacitor C, a resistor of resistance R and an ideal battery of emf V, as shown in figure is known as RC series circuit.
As soon as the circuit is completed by closing key \(\mathrm{S_1}\) (keeping \(\mathrm{S_2}\) open) charges begin to flow between the capacitor plates and the battery terminals. The charge on the capacitor increases and consequently the potential difference \(V_c\) (= q/C) across the capacitor also increases with time. When this potential difference equals the potential difference across the battery, the capacitor is fully charged (Q = VC). During this process of charging, the charge q on the capacitor changes with time t as
\(q = Q[1 - e^{-t/RC}]\)
The charging current can be obtained by differentiating it and using \(\frac{d}{dx}(e^{mx}) = m e^{mx}\).
Consider the case when R = 20 k\(\Omega\), C = 500 \(\mu\)F and V = 10 V.

questions.stem:
(i) (1) What are coherent sources ? Why are they necessary for observing a sustained interference pattern ?
(2) Lights from two independent sources are not coherent. Explain.
(ii) Two slits 0.1 mm apart are arranged 1.20 m from a screen. Light of wavelength 600 nm from a distant source is incident on the slits.
(1) How far apart will adjacent bright interference fringes be on the screen ?
(2) Find the angular width (in degree) of the first bright fringe.
questions._flag: MARKING NOTE (not a void) - under sub-part (ii)(2) the scheme prints 'Give full marks if the student writes the answer in radians only.' That is CONDITIONAL latitude about the unit of a correct answer, not an award regardless of correctness, so it is recorded here rather than in _cbseVoided. Note the question itself asks for the angular width 'in degree'.

questions.stem:
(i) Define a wavefront. An incident plane wave falls on a convex lens and gets refracted through it. Draw a diagram to show the incident and refracted wavefront.
(ii) A beam of light coming from a distant source is refracted by a spherical glass ball (refractive index 1.5) of radius 15 cm. Draw the ray diagram and obtain the position of the final image formed.
questions._flag: CHAPTER NOTE - this question straddles two chapters. Sub-part (i) is Huygens' wavefront construction (Wave Optics); sub-part (ii) is successive refraction at two spherical surfaces of a glass sphere, which is Ray Optics and Optical Instruments / 'Refraction at Spherical Surfaces and by Lenses', and the marking scheme solves it that way. Filed on Wave Optics / Huygens Principle to keep it on the same chapter as the alternative it replaces, Q31(a), which is wholly Wave Optics.

questions.subtopic: Potential Energy of a System of Charges
questions.stem:
(i) Two point charges 5 \(\mu\)C and \(-1\) \(\mu\)C are placed at points \((-3\ \text{cm}, 0, 0)\) and \((3\ \text{cm}, 0, 0)\) respectively. An external electric field \(\vec{E} = \frac{A}{r^2}\hat{r}\) where \(A = 3 \times 10^5\) Vm is switched on in the region. Calculate the change in electrostatic energy of the system due to the electric field.
(ii) A system of two conductors is placed in air and they have net charge of \(+80\mu\)C and \(-80\mu\)C which causes a potential difference of 16 V between them.
(1) Find the capacitance of the system.
(2) If the air between the capacitor is replaced by a dielectric medium of dielectric constant 3, what will be the potential difference between the two conductors ?
(3) If the charges on two conductors are changed to \(+160\) \(\mu\)C and \(-160\) \(\mu\)C, will the capacitance of the system change ? Give reason for your answer.

(i) Consider three metal spherical shells A, B and C, each of radius R. Each shell is having a concentric metal ball of radius R/10. The spherical shells A, B and C are given charges \(+6q\), \(-4q\), and \(14q\) respectively. Their inner metal balls are also given charges \(-2q\), \(+8q\) and \(-10q\) respectively. Compare the magnitude of the electric fields due to shells A, B and C at a distance 3R from their centres.
(ii) A charge \(-6\) \(\mu\)C is placed at the centre B of a semicircle of radius 5 cm, as shown in the figure. An equal and opposite charge is placed at point D at a distance of 10 cm from B. A charge \(+5\) \(\mu\)C is moved from point 'C' to point 'A' along the circumference. Calculate the work done on the charge.
questions._flag: NOTATION MISMATCH IN THE SOURCE, transcribed as printed - the STEM of (ii) gives the charges in microcoulombs (\(-6\) \(\mu\)C at B, an equal and opposite charge at D) while the FIGURE labels the same two charges \(+6q\) and \(-6q\). The signs and positions agree, and the marking scheme works in microcoulombs; only the unit symbol on the drawing differs. Not repaired in either direction.
questions._figure: REQUIRED - sub-part (ii) says 'as shown in the figure' and the stem never says where C and A lie, which is the whole of the potential difference the work done depends on. Read on THIS paper's own page: a horizontal straight line carrying four labelled points, in the printed left-to-right order D, C, B, A, with a semicircular arc drawn above the line from C round to A; the charge \(+6q\) is marked at D and the charge \(-6q\) is marked at B. Deliberately WITHHELD: the spacings between the four points as drawn. Page idx 22.

questions.subtopic: Magnetic Force and Motion in a Magnetic Field
questions.stem:
(i) A proton moving with velocity \(\vec{V}\) in a non-uniform magnetic field traces a path as shown in the figure.
The path followed by the proton is always in the plane of the paper. What is the direction of the magnetic field in the region near points P, Q and R ? What can you say about relative magnitude of magnetic fields at these points ?
(ii) A current carrying circular loop of area A produces a magnetic field B at its centre. Show that the magnetic moment of the loop is \(\frac{2\mathrm{BA}}{\mu_0}\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{A}}{\pi}}\).
questions._figure: REQUIRED - sub-part (i) asks for the field direction and the relative field magnitudes at three points that exist only in the drawing. Read on THIS paper's own page: a shaded circle carrying a '+' sign, representing the proton, at the left, with a velocity vector \(\vec{V}\) labelled beside it; from it a path runs to the right, straight at first to a marked point P, then curving through a marked point Q up to a marked point R near the top, and falling away to the right beyond R. Deliberately WITHHELD: the sense in which the path curves at each point and how tightly it is curved there - the first is what fixes the field's direction into or out of the page and the second is what fixes the ordering of the field magnitudes, i.e. both of the things the question asks for. Page idx 22.

questions.subtopic: Torque on a Current Loop and Magnetic Dipole
questions.stem:
(i) Derive an expression for the torque acting on a rectangular current loop suspended in a uniform magnetic field.
(ii) A charged particle is moving in a circular path with velocity \(\vec{V}\) in a uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\). It is made to pass through a sheet of lead and as a consequence, it looses one half of its kinetic energy without change in its direction. How will (1) the radius of its path (2) its time period of revolution change ?
